title: The Two Watches
synopsis: Kim Gu and a young man, Yun Bong-gil, ate breakfast, then swapped watches.
Now Kim Gu will not say a word. What happened, and why?
goal: Find out what happened at breakfast, whose watch Kim Gu holds, and why, so Haesu's record is true.

options.label: Mr. Kim sits alone with a watch

notes: Haesu's note, read out of order with first, after, before that and at the end. Buying the watch is a decoy her note rules out (not this morning).
Breakfast, then the swap, is history (h2); Haesu, her note and the room are made up.

learning.objective: first, after breakfast, before that, at the end를 읽고 그날 아침의 네 장면을 순서대로 놓는다.
expressions: After breakfast, they swapped their watches.
Before that, Mr. Yun said goodbye.

play.title: Breakfast for Two
story: At the door, a young man in a grey suit passes you.
Inside, two rice bowls are empty on the table.
Haesu gives you her note. "I wrote it fast. It is all mixed up."
play.letter:
At the end, Mr. Kim sat alone at the table, holding a watch.
Before that, Mr. Yun said goodbye.
They ate breakfast first, quietly.
After breakfast, they swapped their watches.
Mr. Yun's watch was new. He did not buy it this morning.
— Haesu
play.question: Put the morning in order, from first to last.
hints: One line says what they did first.
At the end means the last step. Before that means just before it.
play.successMessage: You put the morning in order!
transition: Breakfast, the swap, goodbye, and Mr. Kim alone.
"Mr. Kim is still holding the watch. He has not said a word."
play.orderFeedback: Those are the right steps, but in the wrong order. Read first, after, before that and at the end again.

notes: A picture choice with the names hidden (hideOptionNames): Mr. Kim keeps the watch in his closed hand, and the three pictures are Haesu's drawings in her notebook of the watches she saw this morning. The chain between his fingers rules out the strap watch (and Haesu's own is on her arm); they swapped, so he holds Mr. Yun's watch; Mr. Yun's watch was new, so smooth with no scratches. Told apart by the words (scratches, strap, chain), never by colour alone.
The three watches are drawn plainly (Haesu's drawings), no hands pointing at any readable time, no text.

play.title: Which Watch?
story: Mr. Kim sits by the window. His hand is closed around the watch.
Haesu opens her notebook. "I drew every watch I saw this morning."
"Which one is in his hand now?" she whispers.
play.letter:
Mr. Kim's old watch has a worn case with many small scratches.
Mr. Yun's watch is new. Its case is smooth, with no scratches.
My own watch is small, on a leather strap. It is on my arm.
I can see a chain between Mr. Kim's fingers.
They swapped. Each man took the other's watch.
play.question: Which drawing shows the watch in Mr. Kim's hand?
hints: Read your first clue: what did the two men do after breakfast?
After the swap, Mr. Kim has the other man's watch. What did Haesu say about Mr. Yun's watch?
play.successMessage: Mr. Kim opens his hand: the smooth new watch!
transition: Mr. Kim opens his hand. The watch is smooth and new.
Mr. Yun took the old, scratched one with him.
"But why?" Haesu asks. "Why give away a good new watch?"

notes: Kim Gu retells Yun's words with one word left out. The long hand going round one more time is sixty minutes: one more HOUR (h6: Yun said his watch would be of use for only one more hour). The long-hand line is the game's.
No place, time of day or detail of the act is named: only that Yun would not need a watch after one more hour.

clueInputs.note: Kim Gu holds Yun's new watch: why?

play.title: One More Hour
story: At last, Mr. Kim speaks, very softly.
"Before the swap, Yun looked at his new watch."
"Then he said something I will never forget."
play.letter:
Yun held up his new watch.
He pointed at its long hand.
"When this hand goes round one more time, I will not need a watch."
"My watch is new, and yours is old. Let us swap."
"I will need a watch for only one more ____."
"You will need one for a long, long time."
Then he took my old watch and gave me his.
play.question: What did Mr. Yun say? Write the missing word.
play.prompt: I will need a watch for only one more ____.
hints: Read Yun's words: the long hand goes round one more time.
When the long hand goes round once, sixty minutes pass. What do we call sixty minutes?
play.successMessage: One more hour. After that, Yun would not need a watch.
transition: Mr. Kim closes his eyes. "He knew he might not come back."
"So he gave the good watch to me."
Haesu writes it all down, line by line.

feedback.MINUTE: One minute is one small step of the long hand. Yun said it goes round one whole time.
feedback.DAY: In one day, the long hand goes round many times. Yun said one time.
feedback.WEEK: That is much longer. The long hand goes round one more time: how long is that?
feedback.YEAR: That is much longer. The long hand goes round one more time: how long is that?
feedback.TIME: Close! Which word means one turn of the long hand?

discovery.title: WHY THEY SWAPPED
discovery.detail: Yun gave his good watch away. Now Haesu can write her record.

notes: Haesu asks for proof of each line of her record. The three cards are this case's three kinds of evidence: a witness's note (who saw it, e1), a thing (the watch itself, e2) and words (the reason, e3). Each line takes one, and no card answers two lines. The answer 'why' is the last line proved.
Cards are listed so the right one is never in the same place twice (2nd, 3rd, 1st). After two misses, the tell says what to read again; the right card lights from the third (litAfter 3).

intro: Spring, 1932. Japan has ruled Korea since 1910.
So Korean leaders made a government in Shanghai, China: the Provisional Government.
Kim Gu is one of its leaders. You are his guest.
Early on 29 April, Kim Gu eats breakfast with a young man, Yun Bong-gil.
Then Haesu, Kim Gu's clerk, asks you to come to the house.
"Mr. Kim holds a watch," she says. "He will not say a word."
"Tonight I must write the record of this morning. Help me get every line right."
play.caseSummary: On the morning of 29 April 1932, Yun Bong-gil and Kim Gu ate breakfast, then swapped watches. Yun said he would need a watch for only one more hour. So he left his new watch with Kim Gu. Haesu wrote the true record for the Provisional Government, and Kim Gu signed it. That day Yun acted at Hongkou Park and was caught. After it, Chinese leaders helped the Provisional Government strongly.

notes: PART 4 Case 10: set on the morning of 29 April 1932, around Yun Bong-gil's act, never in it. Haesu and Kim Gu use the season's shared portraits; Haesu's role is told inside this case (Intro).

Yun Bong-gil and Kim Gu are real; most of their words are made up (dossier fiction). Yun's 'one more hour' rests on Kim Gu's account (h6). Haesu, her note, her drawings and her record are made up. The case ends on history: Chinese support for the Provisional Government after 29 April 1932 (h4); Yun's death is told once in the reveal.
